_comment: Tier-2 for sparta rarefied_flow: compute thermal/grid reads far too cold when cells hold few particles, and a fix ave/grid puts it back. Three decks were run on the installed binary (SPARTA 24 Sep 2025, spa_serial), identical argon boxes at 273.15 K differing only in grid resolution so the occupancy falls from 50 to 2 to 0.5 particles per cell while the physics does not change. In the SAME run, the global 'compute temp' stays put across all three while the instantaneous cell-average from 'compute reduce ave c_tg[1]' falls to about a third of it at two particles per cell and to a twentieth below one per cell — because thermal/grid subtracts the per-cell SAMPLE mean and SPARTA writes exactly 0 K into any cell holding one particle or none, and the reduce then averages those hard zeros in. Routing the same compute through 'fix ave/grid' recovers it to within ten percent of the global value at every resolution. All three exit 0 with no error and no warning. Nothing is asserted against a stored temperature: every assertion is a ratio against the global estimator in the same run, or the ordering of three such ratios. COVERS: rarefied_flow:6.
